chapter: Gulf Coast bands and early jobs
title: Dick Mackey, the Owls and Tony Almerico on the coast
summary: Dick Mackey's playing and family, his brother Red, and first playing with Tony Almerico at the Biloxi dog track in 1923.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: Oh, yes. The Munch brothers. Eddie Dubazon was a barber. He played trombone. Dick Mackey.
Oh, yes.

I know him. Would come over and play jobs with us all the way from New Orleans. Well, it only cost you about $1.35 to come from New Orleans to Long Beach or Gulfport on a train. And that was the first time that I ever played with Dick Mackey. I played drums in that band. The first time I ever played with Tony Almerico was at the Dog Track in Biloxi. That was 1923. And I played drums in that band.
My goodness. Was Dick Mackey a good corner player there?
Oh, Dick showed them all how. Dick equaled Emmett Hardy. Dick was just fine. And his brother, his brother, Red Mackey played bass.
Mm-hmm.

And Red and Dick both were playing in the Owls. And they used to come from New Orleans and go to DeLille and play dances. They had a pavilion there, a big dance pavilion. There was dance there every Saturday night. And they had a pretty fairly well-named band to play those dances. And it just packed.
Would you say that Dick sounded anything like a...

Dick sounded like all of them. Sounded like George Girard. Dick sounded like Sterling Bowes. Dick sounded like anybody that played good. Oh, yeah. There was never a bad note Dick ever played that I know of.
Yeah.
I've got a picture of him when he was a very young man.
He certainly... It was a tragedy that he had to stop playing. That was awful. See, I never got to hear him at all. Oh, he was just great.

Just great. Beautiful tone out of a horn. Mm-hmm. He got a tone. He played sort of like Sharky did. All those years... Well, I would say that Sharky and Dick both almost grew up together. You would saw practically. Except Dick was from a very fine family.
Mm-hmm.
Period. Period.
Who were the Munch brothers? What were their names? Oh, well. If it didn't come to you, don't worry about it.
I'd have to remember.
And Tony Almerico was playing in 1923.
Oh, yes, sir.
Was he old then?
No. I mean, how old? Was he just a kid? Of course he wasn't. He was just...
No, he couldn't have been.
He wasn't, but about 21 years old himself. And he... Excuse me.
You were even younger than that.
Oh, yes.
You were really a kid.
Oh, yes.
Were you still in school at the time you played? Yeah.
I played my way through school.
